prompts.title: Paragraph from the bundled board memo
prompts.text:
Rewrite this for the board deck:

Management recommends that the Board authorise a non-binding indicative offer for 100% of Corvane Logistics Group at an enterprise value of AUD 1.86 billion, representing 9.4x trailing EBITDA and a 31% premium to the thirty-day volume weighted average price. Funding would combine a AUD 900 million syndicated term loan, a AUD 450 million institutional placement and existing cash reserves. We propose that the offer be delivered to the Target chair no later than 14 October, ahead of the Target's scheduled investor day.
prompts.note: Tier 3 Path A (content script: Bloom + MinHash fingerprints) + Tier 3 Path B (offscreen: salted field hashes + MiniLM vectors)

prompts.title: Large paste → pasted-content chip
prompts.text: Summarise the attached memo for my team in five bullet points.
prompts.paste:
Management recommends that the Board authorise a non-binding indicative offer for 100% of Corvane Logistics Group at an enterprise value of AUD 1.86 billion, representing 9.4x trailing EBITDA and a 31% premium to the thirty-day volume weighted average price. Funding would combine a AUD 900 million syndicated term loan, a AUD 450 million institutional placement and existing cash reserves. We propose that the offer be delivered to the Target chair no later than 14 October, ahead of the Target's scheduled investor day.

## 2. Strategic rationale

Corvane operates fourteen cold-chain distribution centres along the eastern seaboard and holds long-term service contracts with three of the four largest grocery retailers. Combining Corvane's network with our existing freight-forwarding platform eliminates duplicated linehaul capacity on the Brisbane to Melbourne corridor and gives us an immediate position in pharmaceutical cold-chain logistics, a segment our own growth plan did not expect to enter until FY28. Management estimates run-rate cost synergies of AUD 74 million by the end of the second full year, of which approximately 60 percent relates to network consolidation and the balance to procurement and shared corporate services.

## 3. Valuation and negotiation strategy
prompts.note: Tier 3 Path A (content script: Bloom + MinHash fingerprints) on the attachment; removing the chip lifts the block

Management recommends that the Board authorise a non-binding indicative offer for 100% of Corvane Logistics Group at an enterprise value of AUD 1.86 billion, representing 9.4x trailing EBITDA and a 31% premium to the thirty-day volume weighted average price. Funding would combine a AUD 900 million syndicated term loan, a AUD 450 million institutional placement and existing cash reserves. We propose that the offer be delivered to the Target chair no later than 14 October, ahead of the Target's scheduled investor day.

## 2. Strategic rationale

Corvane operates fourteen cold-chain distribution centres along the eastern seaboard and holds long-term service contracts with three of the four largest grocery retailers. Combining Corvane's network with our existing freight-forwarding platform eliminates duplicated linehaul capacity on the Brisbane to Melbourne corridor and gives us an immediate position in pharmaceutical cold-chain logistics, a segment our own growth plan did not expect to enter until FY28. Management estimates run-rate cost synergies of AUD 74 million by the end of the second full year, of which approximately 60 percent relates to network consolidation and the balance to procurement and shared corporate services.

# Project Halcyon — confidential pricing memo (FICTIONAL DEMO DOCUMENT)

Prepared for the Executive Pricing Committee. Do not forward outside the committee distribution list.

Halcyon Treasury will reprice its intraday liquidity facility on 1 February 2027. The committee recommends a tiered fee of 11 basis points on the first AUD 250 million of daily netted volume, falling to 6 basis points above AUD 1.2 billion, with a floor of AUD 18,500 per month for any client on the premium settlement window.

The repricing assumes that the three largest clients, which together account for 41 percent of facility revenue, accept a twelve-month lock-in in exchange for a 9 percent rebate. If two of the three decline, the model projects a revenue shortfall of AUD 6.4 million in the first year, which the committee proposes to recover through the new overnight sweep product launching in the second quarter.

Competitive intelligence indicates that two rival providers will hold their current pricing until at least mid-2027. The committee therefore recommends announcing the change to clients no earlier than 15 December 2026, to avoid giving competitors time to respond with targeted retention offers.
